facts.fact: The World Bank's diagnostic states that the Ministry of Public Service's Integrated Personnel and Payroll System, a web-based system commissioned about nine years earlier, was implemented in about 200 sites, including all central ministries, agencies and departments and local government; it gives no date, so the publication date is used, and no count of local governments.
facts.system: Integrated Personnel and Payroll System (IPPS) sites in local government

systems.platform: web-based human resource and payroll system
systems.tiers: about 200 sites, including all central ministries, agencies and departments and local government

systems.owner: Uganda Registration Services Bureau until 2016, then the National Identification and Registration Authority
systems.tiers: 202 connected 'online' registration points, against more than 1,400 sub-counties and 345 health facilities where registration was possible, as of July 2012; sub-counties and health facilities not counted apart

systems.owner: sub-county chiefs, town clerks and hospital administrators as registrars
systems.tiers: registers supposed to be kept in 1,403 sub-counties, in towns and divisions and in 345 hospitals; manual and paper-based; legacy records held in local government offices countrywide
117 district offices of the authority, one staff member in each
one floor of the bureau's office and online; seven agencies including Kampala Capital City Authority and the Ministry of Local Government

note: Passages only. The one fact rests on a single sentence placing a web-based payroll system in local government sites; the passages say nothing of how those offices are connected. The 202 online registration points of the vital records system mix sub-counties with health facilities and are left as a systems entry.
